sentences.text: Lymphoma is a group of blood cell tumors that develop from lymphocytes -LRB- a type of white blood cell -RRB- .	white blood cell	white blood cell
The name often refers to just the cancerous ones rather than all such tumors .

Signs and symptoms may include enlarged lymph nodes , fever , drenching sweats , unintended weight loss , itching , and constantly feeling tired .	fever	fever	sweats	diaphoresis	itching	pruritus	feeling tired	Fatigue (medicine)
The enlarged lymph nodes are usually painless .
The sweats are most common at night .	sweats	diaphoresis
There are dozens of subtypes of lymphomas .
The two main categories of lymphomas are Hodgkin 's lymphomas -LRB- HL -RRB- and the non-Hodgkin lymphomas -LRB- NHL -RRB- .

The World Health Organization -LRB- WHO -RRB- includes two other categories as types of lymphoma : multiple myeloma and immunoproliferative diseases .	World Health Organization	World Health Organization	multiple myeloma	multiple myeloma	immunoproliferative diseases	immunoproliferative diseases
About 90 % of lymphomas are non-Hodgkin lymphomas .

Lymphomas and leukemias are a part of the broader group of tumors of the hematopoietic and lymphoid tissues .	tumors of the hematopoietic and lymphoid tissues	tumors of the hematopoietic and lymphoid tissues
Risk factors for Hodgkin lymphoma include infection with Epstein -- Barr virus and a history of the disease in the family .

Risk factors for common types of non-Hodgkin lymphomas include autoimmune diseases , HIV/AIDS , infection with human T-lymphotropic virus , immunosuppressant medications , and some pesticides .	HIV/AIDS	HIV/AIDS	human T-lymphotropic virus	human T-lymphotropic virus
Eating large amounts of red meat and tobacco smoking may also increase the risk .	tobacco smoking	tobacco smoking
Diagnosis , if enlarged lymph nodes are present , is usually by lymph node biopsy .	lymph node	lymph node	lymph node biopsy	lymph node biopsy
Blood , urine , and bone marrow testing may also be useful in the diagnosis .	bone marrow testing	bone marrow aspiration
Medical imaging may then be done to determine if and where the cancer has spread .	cancer	cancer	Medical imaging	Medical imaging
Lymphoma most often spreads to the lungs , liver , and/or brain .

Treatment may involve one or more of the following : chemotherapy , radiation therapy , targeted therapy , and surgery .	radiation therapy	radiation therapy	targeted therapy	targeted therapy	surgery	surgery	chemotherapy	chemotherapy

In some non-Hodgkin lymphomas , an increased amount of protein produced by the lymphoma cells causes the blood to become so thick that plasmapheresis is performed to remove the protein .	plasmapheresis	plasmapheresis
Watchful waiting may be appropriate for certain types .	Watchful waiting	Watchful waiting
The outcome depends on the subtype with some being curable and treatment prolonging survival in most .
The five-year survival rate in the United States for all Hodgkin lymphoma subtypes is 85 % , while that for non-Hodgkin lymphomas is 69 % .	five-year survival rate	five-year survival rate
Worldwide , lymphomas developed in 566,000 people in 2012 and caused 305,000 deaths .
They make up 3 -- 4 % of all cancers , making them as a group the seventh-most common form .
In children , they are the third-most common cancer .	cancer	cancer
They occur more often in the developed world than the developing world .	developed world	developed world	developing world	developing world
